ab8e852d2b8de941e50435b52bde720dda7d027e :
+  /** Patch version for Stan package. */
+  const std::string PATCH_VERSION = "0";

when bin/stanc gets compiled, it isn't picking up the patch-level version number

8a67611678db66b845dd7335b2e60d1e4ade990c :
+* g++ 4.7 not compiling bin/stanc, but OK with models

I am not seeing any problem with g++-4.7 compiling stanc or anything else, except the somewhat random failures we are getting on some bugs models with all compilers.

8a67611678db66b845dd7335b2e60d1e4ade990c :
+* Download:
+  - latest code tarball (named as such)
+    (no git info, but everything else)

It is important to essential that make dist create a "tag" for the git HEAD when it creates the tarball for release. Otherwise, it does not get recorded in git's history when there was a release, and it is not possible to do something like

git checkout version_1.0.0

or to git bisect against 1.0.0 or any number of git things that accept a tag as an argument (which is pretty much everything).

It is possible to overwrite an existing tag with the -f option, so make dist could just do something like

git tag -f $(VERSION)
git commit -a -m "made auto-tag"

before taring everything up. But that generates a lot of noise commits when you are just trying to test that make dist is working properly. It might be better to make a script that calls make dist and uploads the tarball and documentation and whatnot and then that script can handle the git stuff at the beginning.

Ben

On 4/19/12 6:23 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
8a67611678db66b845dd7335b2e60d1e4ade990c :

everything).

git tag -f $(VERSION)
git commit -a -m "made auto-tag"

before taring everything up. But that generates a lot of noise commits when you are just trying to test that make dist
is working properly.

I like your following suggestion better for exactly the reason
you state above.  That's what we did with SVN for our product.


>  It might be better to make a script that calls make dist and uploads the tarball and documentation
and whatnot and then that script can handle the git stuff at the beginning.

The danger is that you forget to tag.

I'm game for whatever makes sense. Part of me doesn't want a make target to automatically do this since the project is open source and curious contributors could end up tagging builds unintentionally. Scripting sounds good. We could also create a Jenkins project to automate as much as we can, including git tagging, tar-ing, etc.

The other option is to do it manually for the first few releases until we know all the steps involved and then script it.



Daniel
